rv.q: In the end, Di and Viv and Rose is a moving and surprising pleasure of an evening, that sends you out into the night with a lump in your throat.
Bullmore hits all the targets Souter aims at, and more.
Bullmore’s play wittily explores its ongoing consolations.
Peter Barnes' exuberant play, which, amazingly, has not had a major revival since its 1968 premiere, fizzes with comedy, ideas and dramatic invention.

cn.t: Critics praise Amelia Bullmore's charming and tender exploration of female friendship spanning three decades, celebrating its comic brio and heartfelt portrayal of a lifelong alliance between three distinct women.
